      Who is reading this?

      The same eighteen parts, three routes through them. Nothing is hidden from anyone; the order changes.

      Read it in sequence

      Each part answers one question, and they build on each other: what exists, how it got here, what happens before the line, how the UK differs inside itself, how it compares abroad, what to build on, and how far to trust it.

                Design documents and traceability

                Solution architecture document (SAD)Context, drivers and components

                Low-level design (LLD)The plan engine and its deadline rules

                Test this with the people who need it

                This guide criticises government for not connecting user research to delivery. This portal has not been user-tested either. Here is the plan it should be tested against, and a way to send feedback from the page.

                  Run the test yourself

                  How this keeps itself in shape

                  Every page verifies itself on load, repairs what it safely can, assesses itself against its own criteria and says so in the footer. An offline harness runs the same checks across every page and writes a report into the pack. What none of it can do is re-request a source, so staleness is escalated by date and stated rather than hidden.

                    Drafft heb ei wirio. Cafodd y Gymraeg hon ei drafftio gan gynorthwyydd, nid gan gyfieithydd cymwysedig. Peidiwch â'i defnyddio fel cyfieithiad swyddogol.

                    • Beth yw hwn Astudiaeth o'r daith gyfan o ddechrau busnes yn y Deyrnas Unedig: o'r penderfyniad cyntaf, drwy gofrestru, hyd at fasnachu a thyfu.
                    • Y dystiolaeth Cafodd 579 o honiadau eu gwirio yn erbyn 953 o ffynonellau. Mae'r gofrestr wirio yn dangos pob ffynhonnell, pob cywiriad, a phob peth na ellid ei wirio.

                    • Y llyfr rheolau Mae 76 o ddyletswyddau wedi'u cofnodi fel data y gall pobl a pheiriannau ei ddarllen, gyda dolen i'r ddeddfwriaeth lle mae un.

                      How to use this, and what it is not

                        Method

                        This guide was built from primary government, parliamentary, regulator, statistical and international sources, graded by evidence tier, with user research and official statistics preferred over commentary. Each page states its own method. Sources were re-requested and headline claims re-matched to their source text on 17 September 2026; the verification register lists every source, claim, correction and note. The assistant on each page answers only from that page's content, and the assistant here answers from a digest of all fourteen. Answers can still be wrong: the sources are the record, not the assistant.

                        Judgements, priorities and proposals are these pages' and are marked as such. Where something could not be verified, the pages say so rather than filling the gap.

                        Not an official government service. An independent, evidence-led guide by Emanuel Silva, part of Public Good Works. Every claim carries its source; check GOV.UK, nidirect, mygov.scot or gov.wales before you act.

                        Drafted and checked with AI assistance (Claude); the author reviewed and is responsible for it. Some features, such as the page assistant, work only inside Claude and are hidden here.
